result.summary: No ship yet. Both round 1 findings are closed, but Table G still permits permanent request loss on mixed nights and overstates what the scheduled alert tells the owner.

findings.title: A / HEAVY — A healthy session disables the halt for broken sessions
findings.body: G4 halts only when G2 equals G1; G6 lets a partial state consolidate. After a Claude field change, one older session with an accepted request alongside newer sessions whose requests are all declined makes G2 < G1. The newer sessions are then marked processed and will not be retried after an update. G3's count is only in the job log. The whole-corpus rename simulation does not test this mixed-version nightly state.
findings.recommendation: Prevent sessions counted by G2 from being marked processed, or halt whenever G2 is nonzero. Add a mixed old/new session test that checks ledger state after the run.

findings.title: B / HEAVY — The digest banner loses the halt's diagnosis
findings.body: The proposed WienerdogError is printed by the dream child, but scheduled `run-job` turns a nonzero child exit into the generic alert reason `job "dream" exited 1`. The digest banner renders that reason and a log hint, not Table G's message. Thus the claimed nightly alert does not say that Claude labels changed or that Wienerdog needs updating; G3 and G4's actionable text remains in the job log.
findings.recommendation: Provide a code-owned, specific failure reason through the scheduled alert path, or state and test that the banner is generic and the owner must inspect the log.

findings.title: B / HEAVY — One legitimate request-less session can halt every night
findings.body: With G1 = G2 = 1, a Claude session containing only a task notification and a concluding reply triggers G4 even if the harness fields are healthy. The halt writes no ledger outcome, so the same unchanged session is selected on every subsequent night; Codex sessions admitted with it are also deferred. The measurement shows this shape was absent from 321 historical reply-bearing files, but does not establish it cannot occur.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish an all-declined user-record session from a session with no request record, and specify a recoverable disposition for a legitimate request-less session. Test repeated nightly selection.

next_steps: Revise Table G and its mirrored tests and owner item before dispatch.
Recheck the scheduled alert end to end, including the text shown in the digest banner.
